title: CPersona recall trace, trace_version 2
description: The trace a recall returns with trace=true (recall), or under trace.recall (reconstruct). It records which rows each stage kept, dropped and reordered, and why, by reference, rank, score and reason; it never carries stored text. This schema fixes the part a failure audit reads: the arms, the fusion, the gate, autocut, the count cut, the held places, the stages and the per-stage input digests. Objects stay open, so a field added later does not break a reader; a field listed here keeps its meaning and type for trace_version 2. Numbers carry four significant digits.

policy.description: The policies the call ran under, by name: `scoring`, and `process` (single-pass-v0 without a time cue, the cue loop's own name with one).

scope.description: The isolation scope the call read.

request.description: What the call asked for and the switches it ran with.

mode.description: The fusion mode: rrf, rsf or cascade.

config.description: The configuration that shapes the result: embedding mode and model, the scan window, the vector reach, whether the fused gate and autocut were on.

arms.description: Each retrieval arm's ranked list as the fusion received it, by arm name (for example vector_near, vector_far, episode_fts, memory_keyword, block, cue). An arm that found nothing is an empty list.

fusion.description: The fused list in fused order, with each arm's contribution where the fusion computed one.

scoring.description: Per-row adjustments a stage applied, by kind (for example prior, episode_penalty), each a map from reference to value.

gate.description: The quality gate. A decision's threshold is its own `threshold` when present, else `thresholds[signal]`.

signal.description: The score the gate keyed on: rsf, cosine or rrf.

reason.description: Why a row that did not pass was dropped.

order.description: The order before the count cut, the count, and the rows the count cut dropped. Empty when the call ended before the cut.

reservation.description: Rows returned in places held beside the count, and the kind of place (block, keyword, far, cue, propagation or depth).

stages.description: The recall process's stages. A call without a time cue is one pass, recorded as stage 0.

suspected.description: Failure codes the server suspected on its own, by stage. A suspicion is not a confirmed code: only a caller that knows the answer confirms one.

stage_inputs.description: What each stage received: how many rows, and a digest of which rows in which order. A replay that starts from a stage checks its input against this; a stage whose input digest matches and whose output differs is where two runs parted.

cue.description: The time cue's effect: the bound it ran under, the rows it moved and the rows it seated.

coverage.description: The coverage ledger over the returned records, recorded after the recall answered.

ref.description: A record's reference as the response spells it.

raw.description: The arm's own score for the row, where it has one.
